label: False killer whale, tag 98364
title: False killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) location data from a satellite telemetry tag (ptt id 98364) deployed in the North Pacific Ocean from 2013-10-23 to 2014-02-23
place: Hawaiian Islands and the North Pacific to the east
method: Wildlife Computers SPOT5 satellite tag; positions by Argos (Doppler)
sample_sentence: This file is the record of one tagged whale. One animal is not a population estimate.
time_convention: Times are as stored in the file: seconds since 1990-01-01 UTC.
location_uncertainty: an Argos quality class per fix; an error radius for 6% of the file's rows, not shown
licence: CC0 1.0 on the data.gov and OBIS records; the file's own terms ask that ATN or the citation be acknowledged
paper_citation_as_given: Project named in the file: Odontocete Tagging in the Main Hawaiian Islands, 2007-2025.

land_data.source: Natural Earth 1:10m land polygons, github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector at commit ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19 (VERSION 5.2.0-pre)

accuracy_note: Positions are Argos satellite fixes. Each carries a quality class. The satellite system's nominal error estimates are under 250 m (class 3), 250–500 m (2), 500–1,500 m (1) and over 1,500 m (0); classes A and B have no estimate. These are nominal estimates, not guaranteed limits: real errors can be larger.
simplification: filtered, not thinned or smoothed: see the stages

rule.speed_limit_source: the tagging group's stated maximum rate of movement for this species in its own filter (Baird et al. 2011 report); a sourced parameter, not a proven speed ceiling

stages.stage: rows that did not pass the data centre's time, location and speed checks
Argos class Z (marked invalid by the satellite system)
speed consistency (experimental rule; limit 20 km/h; classes 3 2 first)
more than 72 hours from any other kept fix
on land in the pinned Natural Earth 1:10m land file

gap_rule.statement: Mother Earth does not join fixes more than 6 hours apart, or where the line would cross land in its land map. These are display rules of Mother Earth's, not part of the study.

card.note: Recorded Argos satellite fixes of one false killer whale, 23 Oct 2013 to 12 Feb 2014, after filtering. A dated replay, not current. Experimental. Private preview.
card.shown: 661 recorded fixes of one whale (tag 98364). 54% of them are Argos classes 0, A or B.
card.done: Shown: Argos fixes that passed the data centre's time, location and speed checks. Mother Earth then left out 1 fix the satellite system marks invalid, 30 fixes under its own speed-consistency rule (20 km/h, favouring better-rated fixes; an experimental rule that can remove a correct fix), 2 fixes more than 72 hours from any other, and 0 on land in Natural Earth's 1:10m map. 661 are shown. Fixes more than 6 hours apart are not joined (0 joining lines refused for crossing land).
card.line: The line joins recorded fixes no more than 6 hours apart: 554 of 660 steps. It is not the whale's route.
card.not_route: Recorded Argos fixes after filtering. Not a reconstruction of where the whale went. The file's last fixes, to 22 Feb 2014, stand alone in time and are left out, so the replay ends 12 Feb 2014.
card.changes: Changes made: fixes left out by the stages listed; the tagging position is not part of the track (its time in the file is eight hours before the file's own deployment start); nothing moved, smoothed or interpolated.
